title: Build a Mini MapReduce Engine
summary: Simulate the MapReduce execution model in pure Python: split the input, run map tasks, shrink their output with a combiner, route keys with a stable partitioner, shuffle and sort by key, and reduce. Then measure how much a combiner saves on the wire.

hints.test_partitioner_is_stable_crc32: Use zlib.crc32(str(key).encode('utf-8')) % num_reducers. Python's built-in hash() of a str is salted per process, so two machines would disagree about who owns a key.
hints.test_split_input_contiguous_and_balanced: divmod(len(records), num_splits) gives a base size and a remainder. The first `remainder` splits get one extra record. Always return exactly num_splits lists.
hints.test_word_count_matches_counter: Lower-case each line and split on whitespace. Every word must end up on exactly one reducer, and the output is the reducers' outputs concatenated in reducer order.
hints.test_each_key_lands_on_exactly_one_reduc: Send every shuffled pair to buckets[partition_for(key, num_reducers)]. reducer_input_records[i] is the number of pairs reducer i received.
hints.test_reducer_input_is_sorted_by_key: After grouping a reducer's bucket by key, call the reducer for keys in sorted(...) order. Keep values in arrival order: map task order, then emission order.
hints.test_combiner_reduces_shuffle_volume: Apply the combiner inside each map task, before partitioning: group that task's output by key (keys in sorted order) and replace it with combiner(key, values). Count shuffle_records and shuffle_bytes (record_size) after the combiner.
hints.test_mean_via_sum_and_count_is_exact: A mean of partial means is wrong when partitions differ in size. Carry (sum, count) pairs through the combiner and divide only in the reducer.
hints.test_inverted_index: The mapper emits (word, doc_id) once per distinct word in the document. The reducer returns the sorted list of distinct doc ids.
hints.test_inputs_not_mutated_and_deterministi: Build new lists instead of modifying the input. With crc32 partitioning and sorted keys, two runs must produce identical results.
